solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Winter travel to which there's no end of cunning

indicators.note: the word for cunning loses its final letter, as 'no end of' asks

parts.note: sleight, as in sleight of hand, is crafty skill or cunning

explanation.surface: A winter journey is so tricky there seems no end to the cunning it needs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no end of' cuts the last letter, T, from SLEIGHT.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse-drawn sledge on snow is a classic means of winter transport.

clue.text: Little influence of surroundings and still less temperature — and there won't be more!

indicators.note: a 'little' version of the word is a shortened one, so only its opening survives

parts.note: atmosphere is the mood or influence a setting exerts

indicators.note: shortened even further than the first word, so only the opening letter of temperature is kept

explanation.surface: A wry remark that the surroundings matter little and the temperature even less, followed by a sigh of finality.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Little' trims ATMOSPHERE to ATMOS; 'still less' trims temperature harder, to its first letter T.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means 'as an upper limit', so there will be no more than that amount.

clue.text: Here I'm rightly looking down on you

definitions.text: Here I'm rightly looking down on you

parts.words: Here I'm rightly looking down on you
parts.note: the speaker occupies a position of ethical superiority, literally a raised spot from which to look down on others

explanation.surface: A smug speaker announces from on high that their disdain is justified.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry the phrase also stands vertically, 'looking down' on the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking an ethically superior position lets one look down on others while feeling in the right.

clue.text: Fringe stuff seen in West?

indicators.note: one word is seen inside the other, so it is placed within it

parts.note: Mae West, the American film actress
to stuff is to cram

explanation.surface: A question whether this marginal material appears in the West.
explanation.walkthrough: 'West' looks like a compass point but is the film star Mae West; 'seen in' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Knotted string work is the traditional craft for making decorative fringes, so it stands for fringing.

clue.text: Caterers scrutinised very carefully? No!

indicators.note: the letters are handled anything but carefully, so they are jumbled

explanation.surface: A rhetorical question whether caterers are closely inspected, answered with a firm no.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carefully? No!' says the letters of SCRUTINISED VERY are treated carelessly, i.e. rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Catering is a prime example of the business sector supplying services rather than goods.

clue.text: Autumn accommodation for belly-flopper will have no effect

parts.note: fall is the American word for autumn
a flat is an apartment, a form of housing

explanation.surface: An autumn lodging for someone who hits the water belly-first turns out to be pointless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for belly-flopper' is extra colour: a belly-flopper lands prone, which is the literal sense of the phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: A joke or plan that misses its mark is said to land with a thud, producing no result.

clue.text: I mention divers without wasting a second

indicators.note: divers is an old word for various or assorted, so the letters are sorted differently

explanation.surface: Someone brings up a group of divers who move with great speed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'divers' is not swimmers but the archaic adjective 'various', signalling a rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means very quickly, almost instantly, with no delay at all.

clue.text: The Thunderer enters answer to claim in excess

indicators.note: one piece goes into the other

parts.note: a plea is a defendant's answer to a charge in court
Thor is the Norse god of thunder

explanation.surface: The Times, nicknamed The Thunderer, responds to a claim with an excessive reply.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Thunderer' was a nickname of The Times newspaper, but here it is the god THOR.
explanation.definitionFit: An overabundance or surplus is a superfluity of something.

clue.text: The keeper of the castle's not to seduce this woman

indicators.note: the seduction word is removed, being 'not' part of what remains

parts.note: a chatelaine is the mistress of a castle or large house, keeper of its keys
to chat up is to try to seduce, so chat stands for it

explanation.surface: The lady of the castle is warned off seducing a particular woman.
explanation.walkthrough: CHATELAINE minus CHAT leaves a woman's name, also that of an Arthurian maid who loved Lancelot.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a female first name, so it denotes a particular lady.

clue.text: My French horn

definitions.meaning: in French the horn instrument is called by this word

explanation.surface: Someone claims a French horn as their own.
explanation.walkthrough: 'My' is not possessive but the exclamation 'My!'; in Britain Cor! is a slang exclamation of surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: It is both a British exclamation of amazement and the French name of the brass instrument.

clue.text: Cross borne by someone of '18', maybe a bull-headed individual

indicators.note: the cross is carried within the other word

parts.note: 18-across is SIXTEEN, and someone aged sixteen is a minor
a tau is a T-shaped cross

explanation.surface: A cross is carried by a teenager, perhaps a stubborn character.
explanation.walkthrough: '18' refers to the answer to 18-across. 'Bull-headed' looks like 'obstinate', but means literally having a bull's head.
explanation.definitionFit: The Cretan monster of Greek myth had a man's body and a bull's head.

clue.text: Two wings linked, playing a neat and simple thing

parts.note: in heraldry a vol is a pair of wings joined at the base
a team playing another is shown as 'v', for versus
neat is an old word for cattle, so an ox

explanation.surface: Two wings joined together play a tidy, uncomplicated game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'neat' is not tidy but cattle; 'playing' gives V as in 'Arsenal v Spurs'.
explanation.definitionFit: This green freshwater alga forms spherical colonies, a simple organism studied in biology.

clue.text: Unnamed person has to develop a raincoat wanted by everyone in Intelligence

indicators.note: the string of pieces is placed inside the word for intelligence

parts.note: wit is mental sharpness
to hatch a plan is to develop it
a mac is a mackintosh, a raincoat
all means everyone

explanation.surface: An anonymous figure must devise a raincoat that every spy wants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Intelligence' suggests spies and secret services, but it is cleverness, the container wrapped round the rest; 'in' signals the insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: The colloquial word is used for someone or something whose name escapes the speaker.

clue.text: Look warm and dry

definitions.meaning: a look or manner, as in 'an ... of confidence'
to expose laundry to warmth so it dries out fully

explanation.surface: An instruction to look somewhere warm and dry.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun means appearance or bearing; the verb means to finish drying clothes in a warm place.

clue.text: Jumble fundraiser's acquired through gambling game

indicators.note: the fundraiser is taken right into the middle of the game

parts.note: faro is an old card game played for stakes
a rag is a British student charity fundraising event

explanation.surface: A jumble sale raises money through a game of chance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jumble' suggests a jumble sale, but is the definition. A RAG is a British student charity fundraising week.
explanation.definitionFit: A confused mixture or hotchpotch of things is a muddle.

clue.text: Our Vera and I, besotted for so long

indicators.note: being besotted is being muddled or infatuated, so the letters are confused

explanation.surface: Two people, Vera and the speaker, have been infatuated for ages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'so long' looks like a length of time but is a farewell.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are ways of saying goodbye, one English slang, one French.

clue.text: M-madness?

parts.note: M names a British motorway, such as the M1, and the madness is the fury of drivers on it

explanation.walkthrough: In Britain motorways are numbered M1, M25 and so on, so 'M' stands for motorway; the stammered 'M-' adds a touch of temper.
explanation.definitionFit: Violent anger shown by motorists toward others is a kind of driving fury.

clue.text: Nurse outside exit waving goodbye to French people in the grid?

indicators.note: the nurse abbreviation goes round the other piece

parts.note: SEN was a State Enrolled Nurse in Britain

indicators.note: a French exit is leaving without a goodbye; this one waves goodbye, so the word exit is altered

explanation.surface: A nurse stands outside an exit, waving farewell to some French visitors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'waving goodbye to French' signals rearranging the exit word; 'outside' wraps the nurse round it. The question mark flags a self-referential, puzzle-specific definition, as with '18' in 11-across.
explanation.definitionFit: The number is presented as a count of entries in the grid, a puzzle-specific tally.

clue.text: I'm partially responsible for giving Samuel instruction

definitions.text: I'm partially responsible for giving Samuel instruction

indicators.note: only part of the words is used, so the answer lies inside them

explanation.surface: A biblical priest claims some credit for teaching the young Samuel.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters sit across 'SamuEL Instruction'. In the Bible, the priest at Shiloh raised and taught the boy Samuel.
explanation.definitionFit: The Old Testament priest brought up the prophet Samuel in the temple.

clue.text: Article pocketed by those playing a game

indicators.note: the article is held inside the word for performers

parts.note: the cast is the actors playing the roles
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: An item is pocketed by the players during a game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pocketed by' looks like billiards or theft, but it signals one piece going inside another; the actors' word splits after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A rummy-type card game played with two packs is one example of a game.

clue.text: A youngster sent right-angled card?

indicators.note: sent here means sent flying or scrambled, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A child receives an oddly shaped card in the post.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sent' looks like posting but signals rearranging the fifteen letters of RIGHT-ANGLED CARD.
explanation.definitionFit: A grandchild's child is a youngster two generations below the grandparent.

clue.text: Prison, in this case, we hope, for what wife-beater did?

definitions.text: Prison, in this case, we hope
definitions.meaning: an old word meaning to this place, here the jail the speaker hopes the abuser comes to
read as two words, the abuser struck the woman

explanation.surface: A grim hope that a wife-beater ends up in jail for what he did.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as two words, the answer describes the assault; as one word it means 'to here', the prison in this case.
explanation.definitionFit: The archaic adverb means to this place, which in the clue's scene is the prison.

clue.text: Ready for walkies and trick?

definitions.meaning: a dog with its leash attached is ready for a walk
to deceive or string someone along

explanation.surface: A dog is ready for a walk and to perform a trick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'walkies' is British for a dog's walk.
explanation.definitionFit: A dog with its leash attached is ready; to string someone along is to deceive them.

clue.text: Fatigue finished con

parts.note: over means ended
to do someone is to swindle them

explanation.surface: A tired con artist has finished a swindle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fatigue' is a verb here: to wear out by too much effort.
explanation.definitionFit: To exhaust someone through excess exertion is to tire them out.

clue.text: One unsettled in atlas?

parts.note: a means one

indicators.note: the letters are disturbed into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone feels lost or out of place within the pages of an atlas.
explanation.walkthrough: An inhabitant of Alsace, a region long passed between France and Germany, is someone from an unsettled place in the atlas.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of Alsace is called by this name, and the region's nationality shifted repeatedly.

clue.text: Raises litter after the first perishes

indicators.note: the opening letter of the litter word dies away

parts.note: a litter of young dogs are pups

explanation.surface: A litter grows after its first member dies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'litter' means young animals, not rubbish; PUPS loses its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb, it means increases or lifts, as in 'ups the price'.

clue.text: Sign a man of Rome has spirit

parts.note: vir is Latin for man
gin is a spirit

explanation.surface: A Roman man shows he has courage, a sign of character.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spirit' looks like courage but is the drink.
explanation.definitionFit: The zodiac sign Virgo is pictured as a maiden, so the sign is named by this word.

clue.text: Aroused, suddenly attacked reduced number?

explanation.surface: Something about an excited person being ambushed, and a shrunken number.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reduced number?' adds a third cryptic reading: NO, short for number, turned round gives ON.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both to excite and to round on someone in hostility.
